content.user_title: Apply Aeon Time Series Machine Learning
content.value_statement: Time series projects need methods that handle temporal shape, distance, and sequence structure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Aeon workflows for modeling, forecasting, anomaly detection, and benchmarking.
actual_capabilities: Select Aeon classifiers, regressors, clusterers, forecasters, anomaly detectors, and segmenters for time series tasks.
Prepare data in Aeon collection shapes and apply normalization, imputation, scaling, and feature extraction.
Use ROCKET, MiniRocket, Catch22, shapelet, distance-based, and deep learning approaches from Aeon references.
Build sklearn-compatible pipelines that combine Aeon transformers with standard estimators.
Evaluate models with task-specific metrics for forecasting, clustering, segmentation, and anomaly detection.
Load benchmark datasets and compare results against published Aeon benchmark tables.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples, but it does not include executable automation files.
Users must install Aeon and any optional dependencies in their own Python environment.
Deep learning examples may need larger datasets, GPUs, and longer training time.
Model quality still depends on clean data, correct labels, and suitable validation design.

use_cases.title: Classify Sensor Signals
use_cases.description: Choose and evaluate Aeon classifiers for labeled sensor, device, or process-monitoring time series.

use_cases.title: Find Temporal Anomalies
use_cases.description: Use matrix profile and anomaly detection methods to identify unusual subsequences or operating states.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Forecasting Workflows
use_cases.description: Compare forecasting models, metrics, and validation choices before selecting a production approach.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starter Model
prompt_templates.prompt: I have univariate labeled time series. Recommend an Aeon classifier, explain the input shape, and list the first validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Classification Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Aeon workflow for time series classification with normalization, a ROCKET-based model, accuracy evaluation, and baseline comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Detect Anomalies in Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me use Aeon to detect anomalies in a long sensor sequence. Include window selection, score thresholding, and validation advice.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Benchmark Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Aeon benchmark for classification, forecasting, and segmentation across multiple datasets. Include metrics, statistical tests, and reporting structure.

output_examples.input: Recommend an Aeon classifier for a small labeled dataset with warped patterns.
output: Start with a distance-based nearest-neighbor classifier using DTW.
Normalize each series before training and keep a simple Euclidean baseline.
Use cross-validation because small datasets can produce unstable holdout scores.

output_examples.input: Plan anomaly detection for a single long machine vibration signal.
output: Use a matrix profile detector such as STOMP with a window based on one operating cycle.
Inspect the highest anomaly scores and compare them with known maintenance events.
Tune the threshold with labeled events or a reviewed sample of normal periods.

output_examples.input: Improve a forecasting workflow with Aeon metrics.
output: Evaluate absolute error, squared error, and percentage error where values are nonzero.
Use rolling or blocked validation to avoid leakage from future observations.
Compare the selected model against simple seasonal and naive baselines.

best_practices: Normalize or scale time series before using distance-based, convolution-based, or feature extraction methods.
Start with simple baselines and ROCKET-style models before using deep learning architectures.
Use validation splits that preserve time order and prevent future data leakage.
anti_patterns: Training deep learning models on very small datasets without a simpler baseline.
Mixing train and test data during transformation, feature extraction, or normalization.
Using standard tabular methods without checking whether temporal alignment or sequence length matters.

faq.question: What data shape does Aeon expect?
faq.answer: Most collection tasks use shape n_samples, n_channels, n_timepoints. Univariate data usually has one channel.

faq.question: Can Aeon work with sklearn pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. Aeon estimators and transformers are designed to work with sklearn-style fit, predict, transform, and Pipeline APIs.

faq.question: Which model should I try first?
faq.answer: For classification, start with MiniRocketClassifier or RocketClassifier. They provide strong speed and accuracy for many datasets.

faq.question: Does this skill run training automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users run code in their own Python environment.

faq.question: How should I handle missing values?
faq.answer: Impute missing values before modeling, then validate that imputation does not leak test information.

faq.question: When should I use DTW distance?
faq.answer: Use DTW when similar patterns may shift or stretch across time. Compare it against simpler Euclidean distance.
